attributes.description: A firewall manager's RUNNING rules read back, read-only, against the record's ciamFirewallRule and what the network-firewall add-on renders (milestone 6.2c, task 529). The add-on's importer (PAN-OS/Panorama first: panos/running-config, from an explicit running-config snapshot or the XML API's action=show envelopes its collector saves) matches rules by the add-on's description marker, then its rule name; it reads sources, ports, protocol and target role into the neutral rule (out-of-band changes are import take/keep conflicts) and records what the neutral rule can't hold as observed attributes: ciamRunningState (committed on a manager, deployed on a firewall, disabled, missing), ciamRunningFact ('<key> <value>': record-owned drift such as action, log-end, destination, description, unresolved members; team settings that limit access such as negation and schedule), ciamUnrecordedRule on the appliance (rules carrying the environment's marker the record lacks, unmarked allows to its servers), and ciamRecordedCidr of external allowlists whose ciamAllowlistRef names an object the export holds. The core (vendor-neutral, for later AlgoSec/Tufin/FireMon importers) reports them: planner check check_firewall_running and report firewall-running.

attributes.name: external_allowlists
attributes.purpose: Specs of other parties' allowlists holding our addresses (80-external-allowlists), each with where it lives in its system when an import can read it (ciamAllowlistRef: hq-apps-egress-to-ldaps on the HQ Panorama's shared address group)

attributes.name: exports
attributes.purpose: {path under exports/: text} built from the estate: directory servers' config/ directories, access logs, what the clouds report (exports/cloud), each provider's region list (exports/regions, estate.region_exports) and quota limits (exports/quotas, estate.quota_exports), the production directory's user data, and the lab Panorama's running configuration as the XML API answers it (exports/panos, firewall_running.panorama_exports)

attributes.name: objects
attributes.purpose: {addresses, services, rules} of env m's firewall rules as the play's vars: source-range address objects (shared names), server address objects named per environment (opsdir-<cloud>-<env>-<server>; UNBOUND when no IP), service objects per protocol/port, rules opsdir-<cloud>-<env>-<rule> in ciamRulePriority order (unpinned last) with marker description and 'after' = previous rule name (None for the first).

attributes.name: observed_rule
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "e", "type": "Entry", "required": true}, {"name": "state", "type": "str|None", "required": true, "description": "a RUNNING_STATES value"}, {"name": "facts", "type": "Iterable[str]", "required": true, "description": "'<key> <value>' facts"}]
attributes.purpose: A firewall rule entry with what a read-back of a firewall manager's running configuration observed: ciamRunningState and ciamRunningFact replaced (none: removed); the rest of the entry kept.

attributes.name: observed_appliance
attributes.purpose: An appliance entry with the rules its running configuration holds that the record doesn't (ciamUnrecordedRule replaced; none: removed).

attributes.name: allowlist_refs
attributes.purpose: The external allowlists whose ciamAllowlistRef an adapter's importer reads ('<adapter>:<path>'), with the path after the adapter's prefix.

attributes.name: recorded_allowlist
attributes.purpose: An external allowlist entry with the addresses its system holds today (ciamRecordedCidr replaced), as a read-back of that system observed them.

attributes.name: running_facts
attributes.purpose: A rule's ciamRunningFact values split into what the record owns (OWNED_FACTS: the next push restores it) and the network team's settings limiting what it admits (ACCESS_FACTS).

attributes.name: check_firewall_running
attributes.purpose: Planner check over the source and target environments' firewall rules as last read back from their firewall managers: missing, disabled, record-owned drift and access-limiting settings per rule, and each appliance's unrecorded rules, as actions; rules only committed on a manager named as fine with delivery unconfirmed. Nothing when nothing was read back.

attributes.name: firewall_running_rows
attributes.purpose: Report source (directory_report firewall-running): per environment, each firewall rule read back (state, what it runs the record doesn't) and each appliance's unrecorded rules, with when the last import covering it read the live system.

attributes.name: rule_name
attributes.purpose: The PAN-OS security rule name the add-on writes for firewall rule r of environment m: opsdir-<cloud>-<env>-<rule>, cut with a digest past 63 characters.

attributes.name: server_object
attributes.purpose: The PAN-OS address object name the add-on writes for server s of environment m: opsdir-<cloud>-<env>-<server>.

attributes.name: marked
attributes.purpose: (environment label, rule, target role) a security rule's description names when it starts with an environment's marker ('opsdir <cloud>/<env>: <rule> -> role <role>'), else None: how a read-back knows which record rule a running rule realizes.

attributes.name: xpath
attributes.purpose: The XML API xpath of one family (pre-rulebase, post-rulebase, rulebase, address, address-group, service, service-group) of one scope (shared, device-group/<name>, vsys/<name>); reconstructed from Palo Alto's documented examples.

attributes.purpose: (Running or None, notices) of one appliance's files: its running-config.xml <config> snapshot, else its api/<scope>/<family>.xml XML API answers; None when nothing can be read or the answers are incomplete (never half a read); DOCTYPE/entities refused.

attributes.name: chain
attributes.purpose: The scopes a rule's objects resolve in, nearest first: its own, then shared.

attributes.name: resolve_addresses
attributes.purpose: ((cidr, ...), (unresolved, ...)) of a rule's sources or destinations in a scope: any = 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0; literals, ip-netmask objects and static groups resolve (recursively, cycles named); ranges, wildcards, FQDNs, dynamic groups and objects not in the export are named.

attributes.name: resolve_services
attributes.purpose: (((protocol, port), ...), (unresolved, ...)) of a rule's services in a scope: TCP/UDP service objects and static groups on single ports resolve; any, application-default, port ranges, other protocols and predefined services are named.

attributes.name: placement
attributes.purpose: (kind, own scope, ((scope, rulebase), ...) in enforcement order, (scope, rulebase) the add-on writes to) of a network-firewall appliance: a firewall's vsys (scope vsys<n>, none: vsys1) or a Panorama device group (shared pre, DG pre, DG post, shared post).

attributes.name: management_host
attributes.purpose: The host name an appliance's management address or a URL names, lower case (no scheme, port or path).

attributes.name: allowlist_place
attributes.purpose: (host, scope, kind, name) a panos ciamAllowlistRef's path names, or None when it isn't <host>/<scope>/<address|address-group|rule>/<name>.

attributes.purpose: Importer panos/running-config: Imported of each <cloud>/<env>/<appliance>/ folder's running configuration against that environment: rules matched by marker then name, sources/ports/protocol/role read into the rule (core.inventory), state and facts observed, missing rules, the appliance's unrecorded rules, and the external allowlists whose ciamAllowlistRef the files hold.

attributes.name: credential

attributes.description: Milestone 102 (6.2c; read it and proposal 3024). Read the RUNNING rules back from PAN-OS firewalls/Panorama (read-only) to find drift against the record's ciamFirewallRule and the PAN-OS add-on's rendered rules: rules changed out of band, rules the record doesn't hold, expected rules missing; external allowlist request status where readable. STEP 1 (now, before vendor facts): survey what the record and packages/opsdir-adapter-panos already hold (render model, names/digests/tags it writes, team-owned fields it keeps, the infrastructure/network domain's firewall classes and checks, existing drift patterns e.g. edge/network imports) and draft the design. STEP 2: the master sends the Codex vendor research (PAN-OS XML/REST running-config reads, auth/least privilege, export format, drift gotchas) as a research note; then escalate the design (kind decision, with recommendation): neutral model (reuse the network/infrastructure classes; observed attributes; RESERVED core numbers 700-709, classes 147-148 only if needed), importer (offline running-config / API export) + read-only collector, matching keys (the add-on's own names/tags/digests first), what drift is reported (planner check + report), showcase story (fixture export, no live calls). Build after the answer. Rules 2991 + 3002. Boundary: core infrastructure/network domains (firewall parts), packages/opsdir-adapter-panos, docs, examples/showcase (ids CHG-2048+, B48+/A145+, data file 27+), tests. NOT the pki domain, cyberark/vault adapters, governance credential schemes or live.py (worker on task 528), not estate/evidence or format-oscal.
